tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

lawrie-model-infinite-square-periodic-gr: Introduction p.2: 'For this work, the metamaterial is modeled as an infinite square periodic quantum graph'; the resonator section p.2 states the open-graph resonator arranged periodically. The paper's own model.
lawrie-unitary-vertex-neumann-lossless-s: Resonator section p.3, Eqs. (3)-(4): vertex mapping is unitary and Neumann conditions are assumed, as the paper states.
lawrie-edge-flux-definition: p.5-6, Eq. (19): J(psi) := Re(conj(psi)(1/i)d psi/dz) = k(|a+|^2 - |a-|^2) defines the edge flux, used to build the Poynting vector.
lawrie-interface-matching-conditions: p.8: the paper enforces k1=k2 and, from periodicity in y, kappa_1y = kappa_2y as the interface boundary conditions of its model; normal components come from each dispersion curve (Fig. 9).
lawrie-interface-two-event-scattering-ma: p.9, Eqs. (32)-(33): the paper defines S_1,2 through Event I and Event II with the stated amplitudes.
lawrie-n-layer-transfer-matrix-method: p.12, Eqs. (41)-(46): the paper defines the layered formalism, the combined transfer operator and the single-point-scatterer matrix S_1,N. The Transfer Matrix Method itself is cited (ref 19); the paper's own construction is what the value states.
lawrie-scope-forthcoming-and-data-on-req: Conclusion p.12 states further results are for forthcoming publications. Data and Code availability p.13 states both are available on reasonable request. No link appears.
sra-design-aim-four-minutes: Section 2 p.4: 'Our aim with SRA is to enable physicians to pose their complex ad hoc questions directly...four minutes rather than four weeks.' A stated aim, not a result.
five-challenges-listed: Section 2 pp.4-6: the paper itself lists Challenges 1-5 with these titles. The value paraphrases them faithfully.
workflow-interactive-clarification: Section 3.1 p.6-7, step 1-2: the quoted sentences describe the system's main process, as the authors state.
fragment-combination-inference: Section 3.1 item 3, p.8: describes SRA's design for combining fragments and the two main decisions, as the authors state.
avoided-sophisticated-parsers: Section 3.2 p.12: the authors state their design choice to avoid sophisticated parsers and give their reason; the value reports it as their stated choice.
expectation-driving-assertions-manual: Section 3.2.2 footnote 13, p.14: states how its own assertions were produced and what could be done for broader applications.
syntactic-temporal-templates: Section 3.2.2 p.14: states the system's mixed templates and gives the example pattern and its temporallyBetween-Inclusive output.
specificity-meta-reasoning: Section 3.2.2 p.14: the paper states the limited meta-reasoning heuristic of its own system and notes it is logically possible but unlikely.
nlg-variable-naming-rule: Section 3.2.3 p.16: states the naming rule (most specific constraint, non-plural noun, unused, at most 30 characters) and the count of 1750 denotesArgInReln assertions in its KB.
fail-soft-not-integrated: Footnote 4, p.6: fail-soft features were in CAE and used experimentally elsewhere but 'have not been integrated deeply into the SRA's initial research cohort selection application'.
domain-scaling-top-down: Section 4 p.19: initial acquisition is done top-down; for cardiac catheterization the first step used Kern 2004 as reference, then expansion from a sample of queries (underway).
future-work-clinical-use-user-model: Section 4 pp.20-22: Clinical Use, user and task models, Smarter Data Entry, and the weak and strong semantic search are presented as future extensions; the weak form 'may succeed or fail based more on the algorithms developed'.
semantic-search-usage-unknown: Section 4 p.22: the authors say they lack preliminary results on how researchers and clinicians will use semantic search and hope to discover it empirically.
fpml-task-definition: Section 2 p.4: 'only one photon-detection event is allowed...hence the name of first photon machine learning' defines the task.
fpml-data-format: Section 2 p.4: 28x28 binary MNIST patterns encoded as spatial modes of a few-photon coherent signal through a binary spatial modulator.
fpml-test-set-1000: Section 3 p.7: 'we consider the first 100 hand-written patterns of each digit...total pattern number is 1000'.
fpml-fair-comparison-constraint: Section 2 p.4: the authors state the design of the CC and QC comparison: same resources, same first-photon constraint, only superposition differs.
fpml-ten-mode-readout: Section 2 p.6: 'In this experiment, we consider the simplest case where the photons are projected onto 10 spatial modes', one per digit class.
fpml-optical-setup: Section 3 pp.6-7: lists the MLL, WDM wavelengths 1554/1564 nm, DMD, SLM with 10 phase masks, PPLN waveguide upconversion and silicon single-photon detector.
fpml-sequential-mask-procedure: Section 3 p.7: the experimental procedure; masks uploaded sequentially, rotation stops at first photon detection.
fpml-slow-slm-limit: Section 3 p.7: SLM refresh about 0.7 fps, 1.4 s per mask, at least 14 s per pattern, actual time much longer; the paper states this limit of its apparatus.
fpml-photon-rate-regime: Section 3 p.7: probe power set so at most 0.1 photon per pulse; 0.001 to 0.06 average for MNIST digits, as the authors state.
fpml-hg-mode-selection: Section 3 p.7: the mode selection rule, the restriction to a dozen HG modes without much optimisation, and the first selected set, as stated.
fpml-cc-computation-method: Section 3 p.8: states how the ideal CC fidelity is computed (index pixels, equal-probability assignment, 1/10 for no index pixel).
fpml-advantage-only-on-average: Section 3 p.8: the authors state the advantage holds only on statistical average and that ideal CC does better for Label 0.
fpml-energy-whole-system-limit: Section 4 pp.9-10: the authors state whole-system energy is much more than 1e-19 when devices and undetected photons are counted, and that more electronics-to-optics replacement is needed.
fpml-narrow-setting-limit: Section 4 p.9: the authors state the advantage is shown in a specifically designed, narrowly purposed setting.
fpml-data-availability: Declarations p.19: 'will be uploaded' to Google Drive, GitHub or another site; the data are over 100 GB. The text states future upload only.
li2024-device-geometry: Section II p.1: Z-cut 600 nm TFLN, 80 um radius, 1700 nm top width, 149 poling gratings, as stated.
li2024-triple-resonance-modes: Section II pp.1-2: quasi-TM modes for d33, triple resonances at 1545.73, 1558.15 and 775.97 nm, and Pulse 1 and Pulse 2 naming.
li-2024-li2024-coupled-mode-model: Section II p.2, Eqs. (1)-(3): the equations are the paper's simulation model (taken from ref 25); the Matlab time-domain solution with cold-cavity parameters and the measured input pulses is its own simulation set-up. The value states only that.
li2024-pulse-and-detection-setup: Section II p.2: 2 ns Gaussian pulses, MHz repetition rate, chosen to mitigate thermo-optic and PR effects; carving, amplification, DWDM filtering and 5.0 dB facet loss are stated.
li2024-normalization-method: Section II p.2: output power normalised to the off-resonance peak power; relative arrival times tuned by AWG phase.
li2024-monitoring-pulses: Section II p.4: describes the phase-matching adjustment and the non-overlapping alternate pulses used as a monitor, as the authors state their procedure.
li2024-data-availability: Acknowledgments p.4: data not publicly available, obtainable on reasonable request; ONR award stated; title block lists Quantum Computing Inc.
li2024-device-g-and-q: Experiments and simulations p.2: PPLN microring on 600 nm z-cut, g = 8.2 MHz, Qi = 7 x 10^5, as the paper states.
li2024-three-modes: p.2-3: quasi-TM modes with signal 1545.73 nm, pump 1558.01 nm, sum-frequency 775.93 nm, as stated.
li2024-table-ii-decay-rates: Table II, p.3: the quoted cells match the values stated (pump external 8.45, total 10.1; sum-frequency intrinsic 2.0, external 12.1, total 14.1 GHz). Device parameters as the paper reports them.
li2024-overcoupled-regime: p.3: states external decay at least four times intrinsic for all three waves; Table II confirms (8.45/1.6, 7.6/1.8, 12.1/2.0).
li2024-cold-cavity-caveat: p.3: Table II measured at low intensity ('cold'); heating may change parameters and phase matching, needing small corrections.
li-2024-parametric-li2024-coupled-mode-m: p.3, Eqs. (1)-(6): the paper defines C_sigma normalisation and kappa_t as intrinsic plus external; the equations are from Chin and Ho (ref 33), which the value says.
li2024-sim-cold-cavity-numerical: p.3: 'With cold cavity kappa_sigma, the simulation results are calculated numerically.' States how its simulations were run.
li2024-experiment-setup: pp.3-4: two Santec lasers, AWG-driven EOMs at 1 MHz pump and 2 MHz signal, EDFAs, WDMs, ATTs, beamsplitter, lensed fiber, TEC at 0.01 C.
li2024-detection-and-losses: p.4: 10 GHz R2860D receiver, 20 GHz oscilloscope, 40 dB/m loss inferred from Qi, 4 mm bus waveguide, 5 dB per facet.
li2024-qcw-signal-prep: p.4: signal is 10 ns quasi-CW at 2 MHz and 0.2 mW; pump Gaussian 2 ns FWHM at 1 MHz centred in signal pulses; quoted power is on-chip peak power in the bus waveguide.
li2024-funding: Acknowledgments p.6: ONR Award N00014-21-1-2898 and fabrication at ASRC, CUNY.

theory_low.lawrie-bloch-secular-equation: Eq. (15) is derived in the text from Eqs. (10)-(14) with Bloch's theorem (a cited standard result), but it is not a stated and proved theorem and not a definition. A derivation shown in running text is not the 'proved result' basis.
theory_low.lawrie-propagating-vs-evanescent-band-ga: p.5: one sentence interpreting real and imaginary kappa_x as propagating and evanescent waves. An interpretation of the dispersion solutions, not defined or proved here.
theory_low.lawrie-empty-lattice-dispersion: p.5: Eq. (18) follows 'By solving Eq. (15)' with the point-scatterer matrix (17); the algebra is not shown, so it is not proved in the paper.
theory_low.lawrie-poynting-vector-normal-to-contour: p.5: stated as how energy flow relates to the contour, and that plane waves need not follow the energy flow. A physical statement without derivation or definition here (Eq. 20 only evaluates J from edge flux).
theory_low.lawrie-interface-flux-conservation-unita: p.9: the reduction (30) to (31) holds only under the scaling choice (29) and the assumption that the normal Bloch wave numbers are real. The value and quotes drop that condition for (31), and the step is asserted, not derived. Not a proved result as stated.
theory_low.fpml-classical-vs-quantum-state: p.5, Eqs. (1)-(2): a qualitative description (which-way information gives a mixture, otherwise coherent paths give off-diagonal terms). Equations are damaged in the text layer and no derivation is given. Not a theorem.
